plan: My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $25 ensures I only win if the prize is worth more to me than what others bid. If I win, I'll pay less than my valuation. If I lose, I miss out on potential profit. With no previous round history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid seems most rational.

My private value is $17. To maximize profit, I want to win only if the winning price is below my value. Since values are randomly drawn between $0-$49, other bidders might have values higher or lower than mine. A strategic bid around my value (but slightly below) could capture potential profit. I'll bid $16.50 - just under my value to create a potential profit margin if I win, while avoiding overpaying.

My private value is $39. My optimal strategy is to bid strategically to maximize potential profit. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, I want to bid close to my value but not exactly at it. I'll bid slightly below my value to ensure potential profit margin. A bid around $35-$37 seems rational - high enough to likely win, but leaving room for potential profit if my value is genuinely higher than competitors' valuations.
